context:
Goal: a lane can fix its own commit on its own branch without stray branches or a second PR.
Problem (rule): auto mode's classifier refuses `git push --force-with-lease` to a lane's own branch as "Git Destructive", yet the force-push guard and lint/check_red_run.py both name that push as the remedy. Three lanes hit it: opus-plain-ask and call-judge-widening (Nov 3), and mutate-guard-cap (02:00 CST Nov 4, which opened PR 1211 to replace PR 1210).
Based on (ruling): stale-safe-force-push allows this push. The owner is asked again only because the change is an auto-mode allow rule, a permission setting that only he grants.
Based on (incident): debt note classifier-refuses-lease-push; closed draft #1191; PR 1210 replaced by 1211; stale branch opus-plain-ask.
Departs from: main, where auto mode refuses every force push — a adds an allow rule for a lease push to the session's own claude/ lane branch only.

lastAnswer.note: Routed 07:52 CST Nov 5 to lane lease-push-c-and-d (same fix as 257) and the coordinator.

options.gain: No stray branches or second PRs; a commit is fixed in place, as stale-safe-force-push already allows.
options.how: Add one auto-mode allow rule: `git push --force-with-lease --force-if-includes` to the session's own claude/ lane branch. It matches stale-safe-force-push; the push guard still asks at the default branch and refuses a lease push with no --force-if-includes or sha. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.
options.label: Allow a lease push to the session's own claude/ branch
options.lose: A lease push to a wrong branch, made by mistake, passes the classifier; only the push guard stops it.

options.gain: Auto mode's list stays as it is.
options.how: No change; each fix goes on a new branch and PR.
options.label: Keep the refusal
options.lose: Each fix leaves a stale branch for your computer to delete, and a second PR.

ref: note classifier-refuses-lease-push; closed draft #1191; PR 1210 replaced by 1211; decision stale-safe-force-push
reply: Moved off the page (your 316 note): your line is in PR #1316, which replaces your #1307.
short: Lease push to own lane branch
title: Auto mode refuses a lane's force push to its own branch, so each fix leaves a stale branch. Allow that one form?
why: Recommended: b, by your question-form rule: an allow-list entry counts as widening a shared tool, and a widening option is never the recommendation. Option a is the coordinator's reading: it only brings auto mode in line with stale-safe-force-push. Meanwhile lanes keep making a new branch for each fix.
